title: Wagner leader Prigozhin claims full capture of Bakhmut after 224-day battle
body:
On 20 May 2023 Yevgeny Prigozhin, head of the Wagner mercenary group, said in a video that his fighters had fully captured the eastern Ukrainian city of Bakhmut at noon that day. He described the operation as having lasted 224 days. Before the war Bakhmut was a salt-mining centre with a population of about 70,000, and the fight for it was described by Al Jazeera as the longest and bloodiest battle of the war so far.

Prigozhin said Wagner would begin withdrawing from the city on 25 May for rest and retraining and would hand control to the regular Russian army. He said five times more of his men had died than should have because of poor support from the Russian army, and he blamed Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov. He acknowledged that Bakhmut had no strategic significance but said it had major symbolic importance.

Ukraine rejected the claim. Deputy Defence Minister Hanna Maliar wrote on Telegram that heavy fighting continued and the situation was critical. She said Ukrainian troops held positions in the city's Airplane area and still controlled some industrial and infrastructure sites. Military spokesperson Serhii Cherevatyi told Reuters that Ukrainian units were fighting in Bakhmut. Al Jazeera said it could not verify either side's claims. Prigozhin had announced the city's capture before, and Russian authorities had not commented on this announcement at the time of reporting.
